original_value: Over the last decade, West African coastal countries, including Ghana, have experienced extensive economic damage due to illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing activity, estimated at about USD 100 million in losses each year. Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing poses an enormous threat to the conservation and management of the dwindling fish stocks, causing multiple adverse consequences for fisheries, coastal and marine ecosystems and for the people who depend on these resources. The Integrated System for Surveillance of Illegal, Unlicensed and Unreported Fishing (INSURE) is an efficient and inexpensive system that has been developed for the monitoring of IUU fishing in Ghanaian waters. It makes use of fast-delivery Earth observation data from the synthetic aperture radar instrument on Sentinel-1 and the Multi Spectral Imager on Sentinel-2, detecting objects that differ markedly from their immediate background using a constant false alarm rate test. Detections are matched to, and verified by, Automatic Identification System (AIS) data, which provide the location and dimensions of ships that are legally operating in the region. Matched and unmatched data are then displayed on a web portal for use by coastal management authorities in Ghana. The system has a detection success rate of 91% for AIS-registered vessels, and a fast throughput, processing and delivering information within 2 h of acquiring the satellite overpass. However, over the 17-month analysis period, 75% of SAR detections have no equivalent in the AIS record, suggesting significant unregulated marine activity, including vessels potentially involved in IUU. The INSURE system demonstrated its efficiency in Ghana’s exclusive economic zone and it can be extended to the neighbouring states in the Gulf of Guinea, or other geographical regions that need to improve fisheries surveillance.

result.paraphrase: Over the past decade, West African coastal nations, including Ghana, have suffered severe economic losses from illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, estimated at roughly USD 100 million annually. IUU fishing is a major threat to the conservation and management of shrinking fish stocks, with wide-ranging negative effects on fisheries, coastal and marine ecosystems, and the people who rely on these resources. The Integrated System for Surveillance of Illegal, Unlicensed and Unreported Fishing (INSURE) is a low-cost, efficient system developed to monitor IUU fishing in Ghanaian waters. It uses rapid Earth observation data from Sentinel-1’s synthetic aperture radar and Sentinel-2’s Multi Spectral Imager to detect objects that stand out strongly from their background through a constant false alarm rate test. These detections are then matched against, and confirmed by, Automatic Identification System (AIS) data, which give the position and size of ships legally operating in the area. Matched and unmatched results are shown on a web portal for Ghanaian coastal management authorities. The system achieves a 91% detection success rate for AIS-registered vessels and processes and delivers information within 2 h of the satellite overpass. Yet during the 17-month analysis period, 75% of SAR detections had no counterpart in the AIS record, indicating substantial unregulated marine activity, including vessels that may be engaged in IUU. INSURE proved effective in Ghana’s exclusive economic zone and could be expanded to neighboring Gulf of Guinea states or other regions that need stronger fisheries surveillance.
